quotes.text: For payments from IBANs outside the European Economic Area (EEA), you must also collect the customer’s billing address, including `city`, `postal_code`, `line1`, and `country`.
You must collect a mandate for each connected account that you process destination charges
You can’t clone SEPA direct debit payment methods and their mandates to connected accounts for use with destination charges.
Stripe can automatically retry each failed SEPA Direct Debit payment a maximum of 2 times, no more than 30 days after the original payment attempt.
Debit failure fees aren’t charged for retry attempts that we initiate automatically.

old_evidence.text: At least 7 business days have passed since the original payment

findings: Both captures describe reusable, delayed, business-initiated EUR SEPA Core with personal and business accounts, no SEPA B2B scheme, no manual capture, and EUR 10,000 each plus EUR 10,000 additional weekly cap for new users. Customer-location property EU and same 40 Stripe business-account locations are separate. Both require additional identity verification after requesting payment-method access. November adds the requirement to collect billing city, postal_code, line1 and country for payments from IBANs outside the EEA, in addition to customer name, IBAN and accepted mandate. The Charge carries Mandate ID (old 6–118, new 7–119). This does not convert the EU customer label or IBAN condition into an individual eligibility guarantee. Source 13–23 omits identity verification and dated address requirement.

Both captures retain Dashboard enablement and Checkout, Elements, Payment Links, Subscriptions, Invoicing, Connect and Express Checkout Element exclusion (old 105–149, new 106–149). Merchant must collect customer mandate before debit; customer can cancel via relevant party or bank and further debits under the canceled mandate are invalid. Stripe learns of external cancellation on a failed payment, then sets inactive and emits mandate.updated. Merchant can also cancel via detachment; after cancellation or deactivation obtain a new mandate before later debit (old 216–224,274–288 and new 222–230,280–294).

Timing stays submission-based T+6 at 00:00 UTC for payment success and available Stripe funds, cutoff 10:30 CET, with later submission for non-business and post-cutoff creation, and five-business-day refusal window after submission. `expected_debit_date` on Charge and listed charge events is estimated when determinable, not guaranteed. Most failures occur within six business days of initiation; rare post-window failures can still appear as disputes. Stripe immediately removes balance funds on failure, with Charge failure_code and failure_message (old 152–162,226–272 and new 152–162,232–278). Source 19 omits T's submission basis and failure caution; line 31 labels its 13 listed codes as 12. Concept 73 and provider index 263 repeat the count. The separate May setup guide 20–27 gives a typical five-business-day arrival figure. Preserve the distinction and timing tension without treating either as external-bank payout or an SLA. Checkout depiction 'payment complete' (old/new 130) does not override delayed timeline.

Both captures require notice for each debit, with Stripe default email and always automatic Stripe email when using Stripe Creditor ID. When allowed to customize, Dashboard versus Sources API controls differ; payment_intent.processing is trigger for debit-initiation emails and required details are listed. Standard is at least 14 calendar days before creation, but the mandate must state any shorter timing. The captured Stripe mandate says up to two calendar days before future payments and allows notice at payment creation. Fixed-amount recurring notices can cover multiple dated debits (old/new 164–180). Source 25 and concept 65 phrase two days as the shortest timing, which misses the cited creation-time case.

Connect continues to require platform enablement plus requested connected-account capability. November adds per-connected-account mandate for destination charges on_behalf_of when that account is merchant of record, no cloning SEPA method and mandate to connected accounts for destination charges, and new PaymentIntent or SetupIntent with on_behalf_of to collect customer authorization. Scope the requirement to the documented destination path without generalizing across charge types. Existing Creditor IDs and name precedence, Dashboard lock after live payments with support migration route, and charge-specific table remain (old 182–214, new 182–220). Source 27/29 and concept 49/69 need these exact actor and Dashboard/support qualifications.

Both captures preserve customer bank no-questions dispute through eight weeks, unauthorized-only up to 13 months thereafter, mandate evidence without guaranteed win, no appeal, dispute amount and fee debited and event, and possible multi-use mandate deactivation (old 274–288, new 280–294). Full/partial refunds up to 180 days, no refund fee but original processing fees nonrefundable, typically 3–4 business days processing and funds within five, credit labeling, and new-account review up to two business days persist (old 290–304; new 298–320). May recommends waiting at least seven business days and mentions a trusted/verified customer, confirmation and accidental debit outreach (old 306–322). November instead advises fully settled original payment, notify customer that refund is being processed and expected timing, and warns disputes can still proceed after refund with double-credit risk; it omits the seven-day number. Keep May advice dated and avoid saying seven days prevents double credit (new 296,310–320; source 39).

November states Radar on by default for all supported payment methods where May said it might default on for Radar users (old 324–328; new 322–326). Both describe real-time SEPA-trained fraud evaluation. November Billing retries heading drops the May private preview label and adds a maximum two automatic insufficient-funds retries no more than 30 days after original attempt and no debit failure fees on Stripe-initiated automatic retries. Recurring subscription invoices and one-off invoices can be enabled separately or together. Do not infer GA or all-account eligibility from missing preview label. November also adds an explicitly prohibited-or-restricted category list in addition to Stripe's general list, including the CBD exception to cannabis wording and payment facilitators processing for sub-merchants; it does not classify every entry individually or negate general Connect support (old 330–332, new 328–351).

Diff 16–42 switches local flow artwork to CDN and retargets the Elements quickstart; diff 56–57 updates rulebook HTTP to HTTPS; numbering, capitalization, table separators and several anchors/labels change without changing their facts. Treat images and linked guides as navigation, not fresh behavioral evidence.

source_assessments.reason: November materially changes address collection, Connect mandate constraints, refunds risk guidance, Radar default, retry disclosures and business categories. Independently correct May baseline failure-code count, notice timeline and Creditor ID lock scope.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sepa-debit, November documents a business-initiated, reusable, delayed EUR SEPA Core debit, covering eligible personal and business accounts rather than the B2B scheme. After requesting activation, merchants complete additional identity verification, collect name and IBAN plus billing city, postal code, line1 and country for non-EEA IBANs, and obtain an accepted mandate. The Charge links the mandate (old raw lines 6-118, new raw lines 7-119). Connect requires platform enablement and connected-account capability. A destination charge on_behalf_of needs a mandate for each connected account as merchant of record. The guide prohibits cloning the method/mandate to connected accounts for destination charges and uses a new PaymentIntent or SetupIntent with on_behalf_of to get authorization (old raw lines 182-224, new raw lines 182-230). Submission time, debit estimate, five-day refusal window, T+6 standard success/funds availability and late failure remain distinct. Customer cancellation invalidates later debits, and a failed attempt can surface mandate inactivity (old raw lines 152-180 and 216-272, new raw lines 152-180 and 222-278). November retains the dispute and refund windows and adds exposure controls, supported-method Radar default and limited automatic insufficient-funds retries. source-stripe-sepa-debit.md broadly preserves May but misses the new requirements and mistakenly labels 13 failure code rows as 12. Setup, modeled payment states and Stripe funds availability are separate from confirmed external payout.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sepa-debit, substantive November 7, 2026 documentation changes include non-EEA IBAN billing address, destination on_behalf_of fresh-mandate and no-clone rules, fully settled refund guidance and persistent double-credit risk, Radar default-on for supported methods, two automatic insufficient-funds retries within 30 days without debit failure fees on Stripe-initiated retries, and added business restrictions (old raw lines 6-16, 182-214 and 290-332, new raw lines 7-17, 182-220 and 298-351). Preserve May's at-least-seven-business-day refund recommendation and private-preview label as dated, without inferring GA or a guaranteed remedy from November wording. Both method captures give T+6 after submission for standard success and funds availability, while the separate May future-setup guide describes a typical five-business-day later-payment arrival. Retain that timing tension, the 13-row baseline correction, and the Stripe mandate’s at-creation notification qualification in source-stripe-sepa-debit.md (old raw lines 152-180 and 252-272, new raw lines 152-180 and 258-278). Image URLs, headings, table formatting and quickstart/HTTPS links are presentational or navigation changes. Preserve the May raw, the root-to-Stripe index and reciprocal Stripe SEPA Direct Debit concept/source route, with acceptance, setup and subscription links separate.
